b: I came across this Ryobi 18V HP limited edition cordless oscillating multi-tool at my local Home Depot store today.
$79 for the kit? That seems like a good deal for a brushless oscillating tool kit, plus you get the blackout edition colorway.
I snapped a photo and then a quick video for cross-posting to ToolGuyd’s Instagram channel.
This was a 1-week deal that expired yesterday. Oh.
Right now, Home Depot has it online for $89.
Is that still a good deal?
I found this Ryobi 18V bare tool selling for $79.
It’s “free with purchase,” if you buy the $99 starter kit with 2 batteries, or the other eligible items.
I then found this kit, with a 4Ah battery and charger, for $79.
And then this 2-battery kit for $99. This seems to be a bundle with the Ryobi 18V cordless power tool starter kit and free tool-only oscillating multi-tool.
I then found this other kit with the same tool, for $99.
I then noticed the Ryobi 18V HP brushless oscillating multi-tool, which is selling for $129. That’s not a kit, just the tool-only.
I had been looking at the wrong tool – this is the correct one! There’s a 1-battery kit for $189.
Ah. The HP version comes with a brushless motor and tool-free blade change.
$79 would have been better, $89 still seems good. Maybe it’ll drop back for Black Friday as a doorbuster.
Now, I definitely feel a bit silly for getting confused. But running into this flood of different options didn’t really help.
The moral of the story: pay careful attention to details when shopping for holiday deals!
A reader pointed out that you can get the limited edition kit plus an accessory set for $87 right now. That’s better than paying $89 for just the kit!
That’s a great example of Home Depot Holiday Deal Math.
